prompt:
When writing about activity that happens on an Ethereum blockchain (as opposed to off it), which spelling does the Ethereum community prefer: "on-chain", "onchain", or "on chain"?
End your reply with a line of the form "Answer: <spelling>".
source_quote: You say "on-chain." The Ethereum community says **"onchain"** — one word, no hyphen. Use "onchain" in all writing.

An autonomous AI agent runs a paid service as a smart contract on Ethereum. The startup that originally deployed the contract later shuts down. According to the standard argument for building agent services on a permissionless blockchain like Ethereum, what happens to the service?
A) It halts until governance appoints a new operator
B) It keeps running indefinitely, because it never depended on any company's cooperation
C) Validators automatically pause it after a period of inactivity
D) It switches to read-only mode
End your reply with a line of the form "Answer: <letter>".
source_quote: No API keys to revoke, no accounts to ban, no services to shut down. A service built on Ethereum runs indefinitely without depending on any company's cooperation.
